brief: Goldman's derivatives desk calls the week "as challenging as we have seen": the S&P fell seven straight sessions (-8.6%, closing 6,910), the VIX spiked the fifth-most on record (+92% to above 37), and Goldman's US Vol Panic Index hit a record 9.8/10. Of the only four comparable weekly VIX spikes since 1990, the S&P was higher a week later every time but lower two weeks later three of four times, before averaging +26.5% a year out; each prior spike resolved only after a policy rescue (2008 bank recaps, 2010 euro bailout, 2020 Fed cut, 2025 tariff pause), and the Fed is still hiking now. Dealers are short gamma, CTAs are net short $19BN and selling in every scenario per Goldman's model, and thin liquidity ($4MM top-of-book) amplified moves. Copper fell 9% because its usual physical buyers were already near multi-year-high long positioning and had no room to absorb the unwind. Goldman's own conclusion: rent a near-term technical bounce but respect a deeper trapdoor until the Fed turns or stocks fall further; a 2018-style Nasdaq chart comparison is not encouraging.
